title: Geometry - Lesson 1 Practice: Circle Area Exploration
description: Practice explaining how sector rearrangement forms the circle area formula.

questions.question: What happens to the total area when a circle is cut into sectors and rearranged without gaps or overlaps?
options: The total area stays the same.
The total area depends on the color of the sectors.
questions.explanation: Cutting and rearranging pieces does not change total area if no pieces are lost, stretched, overlapped, or separated by gaps.

questions.question: In the rearranged sector model for circle area, what measurement becomes the height of the almost rectangle?
questions.explanation: Each sector reaches from the center to the circle, so the height of the rearranged shape is the radius.

questions.question: In the rearranged sector model, one long base is about half the circumference of the circle.
questions.explanation: The curved edges split into two long sides. One side is about half the circumference, which is pi r.

questions.question: If the circumference of a circle is 18π cm, the approximate base of the rearranged sector rectangle is ______ cm. Use π notation.
questions.explanation: The base is about half the circumference. Half of 18π is 9π.

questions.question: Which expression shows the area of the rearranged sectors using base times height?
questions.explanation: The base is about pi r and the height is r, so the area is (pi r)(r).

questions.question: A circle has diameter 12 cm. What radius should be used in A = πr²?
questions.explanation: The radius is half the diameter. Half of 12 cm is 6 cm.

questions.question: Explain in one or two sentences why using more sectors gives a better circle area estimate.
questions.correctAnswer: More sectors are thinner, so the rearranged shape becomes less bumpy and closer to a rectangle. That makes the base-times-height estimate closer to the true circle area.
questions.explanation: The key idea is that thinner sectors make the rearranged shape more rectangle-like.

questions.question: Describe how the formula A = πr² is formed from the rearranged sector model.
questions.correctAnswer: The circle sectors are rearranged into an almost rectangle with height r and base about half the circumference, pi r. Using area = base times height gives (pi r)(r) = pi r squared.
questions.explanation: A complete explanation connects sectors, same area, base pi r, height r, and rectangle area.
